verses.2: I have heard many such words from those who offer hollow comfort, all of you.
verses.3: Is there an end to words that are empty, or why do you press me until I must answer?
verses.4: I also could speak as you do, if only your lives were in place of mine. I could console you with words and ease your suffering with the comfort of my head.
verses.5: I would reprove you with my mouth, and my lips would silence you.
verses.6: If I speak, I will not be comforted, and if I hold back, my pain still lingers.
verses.7: But now you have made me utterly ashamed—my whole assembly, you have become my disgrace.
verses.8: You have become a witness against me, and you rise up against me like a liar, answering me in my face.
verses.9: His fury has seized me and trampled me down. He has bitten into me with his teeth, his eyes have pierced me.
verses.10: They have all turned on me with their mouths, mocking me, striking my cheeks, all of them together turning their faces toward me.
verses.11: He has delivered me to the hands of the ruthless and cast me among the wicked.
verses.12: I was at peace, and he shattered me; he seized me by the back of my head and dashed me to pieces and set me up as a target.
verses.13: His warriors have surrounded me, they have pierced my kidneys, showing no mercy, they have poured out my gall onto the earth.
verses.14: He has struck me again and again, rushing upon me like a warrior.
verses.15: I have torn a sackcloth over my skin, and I have dragged my strength through the dust.
verses.16: My face is red from weeping, and a shadow has fallen on my eyelids.
verses.17: I have not sinned with my hands, and my prayer is pure.
verses.18: Let the earth not cover my blood, nor let a place be found for my cry.
verses.19: Now indeed my witness is in the heavens, and my vindicator is in the heights.
verses.20: My friends, the true companions, have testified to God, and my eye has poured out my pleas.
verses.21: Let a man contend with God, and let a human be justified with his neighbor.
verses.22: For the days of my trial are numbered, and my path will not return again.

notes:
Notes
- v. 13: "poured out my gall onto the earth" — the Hebrew "מְרֵרָתִי" is literally "my bitterness" but is rendered here in a metaphorical sense.
- v. 21: "let a human be justified with his neighbor" — the Hebrew uses "רֵעֵֽהוּ" ("his neighbor"), and the phrase is rendered to preserve the contrast with divine justice.
